conventions: The refrain נִמְשַׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת נִדְמוּ (vv. 12, 20): the Niphal of מָשַׁל and the contiguous comparative כַּ it governs share one unit on the ASV's 'He is like' / 'Is like' under rule 30, since the one word 'like' carries both the verb's lexeme and the kaph's comparison; source head on the verb, target head on 'like'. The assimilated article takes 'the', בְּהֵמוֹת takes 'beasts', the supplied relative 'that' is added (rules 46, 55) because the antecedent is written and נִדְמוּ is a juxtaposed finite clause, and the verb keeps 'perish'.

Impersonal 3mp verbs the ASV supplies a subject for — יִרְצוּ 'men approve' (v. 13), יוֹדֻךָ 'men praise thee' (v. 18) — leave 'men' as its own added unit under rule 17; the verb takes only its lexical verb and any object suffix takes its own pronoun.

A temporal בְּ on a noun with a possessive suffix that the ASV recasts as a finite clause — בְמוֹתוֹ 'when he dieth' (v. 17), בְּחַיָּיו 'while he lived' (v. 18) — gives the subordinator to the preposition (rule 52), the English verb to the noun, and the subject pronoun to the suffix (rule 40).
report: Read all 21 verses end to end against the 23-lemma candidate table and the 13 added units the table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways: every difference in the table is the ASV rendering one word differently in different contexts (suffix case, ki as For/when/Though, waw as And/But/Yet/For/That, lamed as to/for/of), each licensed by the English actually written.

The chapter's two repeated constructions are treated identically where they recur: the refrain נִמְשַׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת נִדְמוּ (vv. 12, 20) fuses the Niphal verb with the contiguous kaph into one unit on 'He is like'/'Is like' (rule 30) and marks the relative of 'that perish' added (rules 46, 55) in both; the impersonal 3mp verbs of vv. 13 and 18 both leave the supplied subject 'men' added (rule 17); the temporal בְּ + noun + suffix recast as a clause (בְמוֹתוֹ 'when he dieth' v. 17, בְּחַיָּיו 'while he lived' v. 18) divides the same way in both (rules 52, 40).

The two גַּם of v. 2 each take the word written for them (Both / and), which is rule 14's two-connective case, not a correlative pair on one morpheme. לָנֶצַח → 'alway' (v. 9, rule 40 fusion) and עַד־נֵצַח לֹא → 'never' (v. 19, rule 35 fusion, corpus heads it both ways and the note says so) differ because the ASV wrote different English, not because the chapter changed its analysis.

BSB disagreements (8): three articles the ASV writes nothing for (vv. 1 vocative, 9 'corruption' bare, 17 on kol fused into 'nothing'), the waw and repeated דֹר of the distributive דֹר וָדֹר → 'all generations' (rule 22), and three prepositions whose objects the ASV promotes or recasts (עֲלֵי v. 11, לָ v. 13, בְּ v. 13; rule 40). All are documented convention differences; none is an error.

Hedged decisions already carry their competing reading in the note (v. 11 matrix 'is' on the subject rather than with the added 'that'; v. 9 second 'That' added rather than a distributed repetition of the waw's; v. 4 'dark saying' headed on 'dark'). Nothing here generalises beyond what rules 30, 35, 46 and 55 already say, so no promotion or amendment.
